newsitem.title: USA: Intel sees Q2 gross margins flat to down.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees Q2 gross margins flat to down.

text.p: Intel Corp on Monday said it expects its second quarter gross margins to be flat or slightly below the 64 percent level achieved in its first quarter ended March 29.
In the second quarter one year ago quarter, Intel's gross margin was 53 percent, and in the first quarter one year ago the gross margin was 48 percent.
Intel also said it expects second quarter revenue to be even with or slightly ahead of the first quarter's $6.4 billion.
Last year, Intel generated revenues of $4.6 billion in the second quarter and $4.6 billion in the first quarter.

For the 1997 year, Intel expects its gross margins to be 60 percent "plus or minus a few points", and after issuing first quarter results, Intel believes the number will be "at the mid- to high-part of that range," it said in a statement.
Earlier, Intel reported earnings of $2.20 per share on net income of $1.98 billion versus $1.02 per share on net income of $894 million one year ago.
The company said capital expenditures for 1997 are expected to be $4.5 billion.
Second quarter 1997 depreciation is expected to be about $580 million and year depreciation is seen at $2.5 billion.
Second quarter expenses -- research and development plus marketing, general and administrative costs -- are expected to be seven to nine percent above first quarter's $1.3 billion.
Second quarter 1997 interest and other income should be about $170 million.
Research and development spending for 1997 is expected to be about $2.4 billion.
The tax rate in 1997 is expected to remain at 35.5 percent.

The company said that it still believes that over the long-term the gross margin percentage will be 50 percent plus or minus a few points. with the gross margin percentage varying depending on product mixes.
In the first quarter, the company repurchased a total of 7.7 million shares of common stock at a cost of $1.2 billion under an ongoing program.

Since the program began in 1990, the company said it has repurchased 92.6 million shares at a total cost of $4.6 billion. In March, Intel's board of directors approved an increase of up to 30 million shares in the company's common stock repurchase program. This increase brings the total authorization to 140 million shares.
